subject: EU debug residency window request for Finovate
messages:
From: Sara Martin <sara.martin@finovate.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short EU residency window request for debug

Hi Ben —

We’re chasing a production issue affecting a small subset of EU customers (EU region, tenant finovate-eu-1). Our SREs have a flaky repro that shows up only when EU token routing is in play; to debug they need a short-term snapshot of request/response traces and some tokenized KV state from the last 48 hours.

Can Redwood make a temporary exception to the tenant-level auto-deletion so those logs (redacted) remain in EU storage for up to 48 hours? We prefer Redwood to host the snapshot in an EU bucket or provide an export we can pull. Security is copied on this thread — we’re happy to follow any constraints (encryption, RBAC, narrow scopes).

I’ve attached a small redacted sample to show the format (debug-log-sample.txt). This is sensitive so we want the shortest window possible.

Thanks,
Sara Martin
Lead SRE, Finovate
security@finovate.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Martin <sara.martin@finovate.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Short EU residency window request for debug

Forwarding Finovate’s request — they need a short, tenant-scoped exception to retention for debugging (EU region). Key asks: 48-hour window, EU-hosted snapshot preferred, minimal scope. Attached sample.

Questions for ops/security:
- Can we provide a timeboxed override limited to the finovate-eu-1 tenant and pin the data to EU storage only?
- What controls do we need to require (KMS key, engineer RBAC list, audit trail)?
- Any legal/procurement paperwork? I’ve attached the SLA-exception-form.pdf placeholder in case we need signoff.

If we approve, I’ll coordinate the export and the deletion confirmation. Finovate is asking for urgency — they’ve got customers degraded right now.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Martin <sara.martin@finovate.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short EU residency window request for debug

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:45 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Finovate’s request — they need a short, tenant-scoped exception to retention for debugging (EU region).

Thanks for the heads-up. A few items we’ll need before approval:
- Narrow the scope to the exact data types/keys required (traces + tokenized KV subset is ok; full request bodies we should avoid).
- Confirm specific engineers who need access (list emails) so we can limit RBAC.
- Export must remain in our EU bucket; if exported to the customer, it must be encrypted with their KMS and we need an audit trail of the transfer.
- Fill the SLA-exception-form.pdf and get Finovate’s security to ack the scope.

Operationally I’m inclined to approve a shorter window than 48h — 24–36h is safer and still useful. If we get affirmative answers to the bullets above I’ll sign off pending Neha’s compliance check.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Martin <sara.martin@finovate.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short EU residency window request for debug

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 10:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads-up. A few items we’ll need before approval: ...

We’ve reviewed the sample and scope. Compliance will approve a timeboxed retention exception under the following conditions:
- Window: 36 hours from the moment data is isolated/exported.
- Scope: EU tenant finovate-eu-1 only; traces and the named KV keys provided in the sample. No full request body exports.
- Storage: data must reside in our EU bucket (eu-1) behind Redwood-managed KMS; if Finovate requests a copy, it must be encrypted with their KMS and a transfer request logged.
- Access: only the named Finovate SREs and two Redwood engineers (jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com) will be granted temporary RBAC; access will be audited.
- Audit & deletion: create ticket FIN-20271102-47 (HubSpot ref: fin-12345) and attach deletion confirmation once window closes.
- Paperwork: Finovate should sign the SLA-exception-form.pdf (attached).

I’m approving this with those constraints. Marissa, Ben — please coordinate the export and ensure the deletion confirmation is posted to the ticket.

Neha Kapoor
Head, Compliance & Privacy
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

---
Ben Carter (on behalf of Redwood) to Finovate: We will provision a 36-hour EU-residency snapshot. Please upload any additional redaction instructions and the list of SREs to the HubSpot record (https://hubspot.com/contacts/finovate-12345) and sign the attached form so we can proceed.
